sounds.name: Metallic Chime
sounds.ref: A patchbay lesson: one module’s oscillator shaking the other’s filter
sounds.blurb: A bright, ringing chime with bell-like overtones that fades slowly.
sounds.how: XM2 is not heard (its LEVEL stays at 0), but its VCO 1 still follows the keys. Its output is patched into XM1’s VCF CV, so XM1’s cutoff moves up and down hundreds of times a second: frequency modulation of the filter. That adds overtones that are not in tune with the note, which is what makes it sound like metal. XM2’s VCO 1 FREQUENCY sets the colour of the chime and XM1’s VCF MODULATION how strong it is.

steps.title: A resonant XM1
steps.why:
XM1 is set up as a resonant, ringing tone with a long fade. It sounds plain for now; a cable from XM2 will make it metallic.
- VCO 1 into VCF +3.5 (pulse 70 %): VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. Right of centre on its knob in the VCF (filter) section sends the pulse, a square at its starting 50 % width.
- FREQ 5.5 (843 Hz), RES 6.5: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, with resonance well up so the cutoff rings when it moves.
- ENV 1 A 0, D 3.0 s, S 0: ENV 1, the loudness envelope, strikes at once and fades over three seconds, with nothing held.
- Listen for: a soft, hollow note that dies away slowly, like a struck bar with no overtones.

steps.title: Patch XM2’s oscillator into XM1’s filter
steps.why:
XM2 plays every note silently, and its oscillator is patched in to shake XM1’s filter hundreds of times a second. That is frequency modulation of the filter.
- ASSIGN UNI: both modules get every key, so XM2’s VCO 1 follows the notes. XM2’s LEVEL stays at 0, so it is only a modulator.
- Cable XM2 VCO 1 → XM1 VCF CV: CV means control voltage. XM2’s VCO 1 output (a sawtooth) goes to the input that moves XM1’s cutoff.
- XM1 VCF modulation source EXT: with the cable in, EXT follows it.
- XM1 VCF modulation +2 (+2.0 oct): how hard XM2’s oscillator moves XM1’s cutoff. Low is a soft chime, high a clanging gong.
- Listen for: the note gaining a buzzy, bright edge. XM2 is at the same pitch as the note, so the extra overtones are still in tune.

steps.title: Tune the modulator off the note
steps.why:
XM2’s oscillator is moved off a whole number of octaves, so the overtones it adds no longer line up with the note. That clash is what makes metal and bells sound as they do.
- XM2 VCO 1 frequency 8.5 (+21 st): a little under two octaves up. 7 or 9, whole octaves, sound tuned; between them sounds like metal.
- Listen for: the tone turning into a bell or chime, with ringing partials that do not quite fit the note. Turn XM2’s VCO 1 FREQUENCY slowly to hear the colour change from gong to glass.

sounds.name: Pad and Bells
sounds.ref: SPLIT: a pad in the left hand and a bell in the right
sounds.blurb: A soft, swelling pad under the left hand and a clear, chiming bell under the right.
sounds.how: SPLIT sends keys below middle C to XM1 and the rest to XM2, so the two modules become two instruments. XM1 is a warm pad: two sawtooths, slightly detuned, with a slow swell. XM2 is a bell: a square with a quiet sawtooth an octave and a fifth above it, plucked by ENV 2 and left to ring.

steps.title: Split the keyboard
steps.why:
SPLIT turns the two modules into two instruments: a pad under the left hand on XM1 and a bell under the right on XM2.
- ASSIGN SPLIT: keys below middle C play XM1, the rest play XM2.
- XM2 level 6.5 (65 %): XM2 starts at 0; this sets the balance of bell against pad.
- XM1 pan −1.5, XM2 pan +1.5: 30 % to each side, so the two parts are slightly apart.
- Listen for: low and high keys still sounding the same, the plain starting sawtooth, until each module gets its own sound.

steps.title: XM1: a warm pad
steps.why:
XM1 becomes a warm pad: two slightly detuned sawtooths through a low filter, both envelopes slow so the sound swells in.
- Saws 80 % and 70 %, +10 cents: the VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) as two saws a few cents apart, so the pad beats and moves.
- FREQ 4.3 (373 Hz), RES 1.5: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, set low for warmth.
- ENV 2 A 610 ms, D 2.1 s, S 60 %: with VCF MOD at +1.5 (up to 1.2 octaves), ENV 2 opens the filter slowly and settles.
- ENV 1 A 770 ms, D 2.1 s, S 100 %: ENV 1, the loudness envelope, swells in and releases over 1.7 seconds.
- Listen for: left-hand chords rising slowly and brightening as they swell.

steps.title: XM2: a bell
steps.why:
XM2 gets a bell’s tone: a square with a quiet sawtooth an octave and a fifth above it. The two together give the mix of partials a bell has.
- XM2 VCO 1 +3 (pulse 60 %), PW 50 %: a square, the bell’s fundamental.
- XM2 VCO 2 into VCF −1.5 (saw 30 %): a little towards SAW, quiet.
- XM2 VCO 2 frequency 8.2 (+19 st): an octave and a fifth up, the bell’s upper partial. 9 (two octaves) is sweeter; 8.5 more like struck metal.
- Listen for: right-hand notes with a glassy interval ringing above them. They still hold while the key is down; the next step makes them strike and ring.

steps.title: Strike and ring
steps.why:
XM2’s filter and loudness are made percussive: struck bright, then left to ring and die away.
- XM2 FREQ 5.8 (1.0 kHz), RES 1: low-pass, fairly soft at rest.
- XM2 ENV 2 A 0, D 720 ms, S 0: with XM2 VCF MOD at +2 (up to 1.8 octaves), ENV 2 opens the filter at the strike and closes it over about three quarters of a second.
- XM2 ENV 1 A 0, D 1.8 s, S 0: each bell note rings for nearly two seconds, then fades by itself.
- Listen for: a bright “ding” that mellows as it rings over the pad. Shorten XM2’s ENV 1 decay and the bell becomes a glockenspiel.

sounds.name: Two-Formant Choir
sounds.ref: Two band-pass filters in parallel make a vowel
sounds.blurb: A soft, wordless “aah” from two filters, each holding one of a vowel’s two main resonances.
sounds.how: A sung vowel is mostly two resonances, called formants, that stay in place whatever note is sung: for “aah” about 700 Hz and 1,100 Hz. UNI plays each note on both modules. Each module’s filter is set to band-pass and tuned to one formant, and neither follows the keys, so the vowel stays put while the melody moves. A single synth would need two filters in parallel to do this; the 2-XM has one per module.

steps.title: Both modules on every note
steps.why:
A sung vowel is mostly two resonances, called formants. UNI plays each note on both modules, so each module can hold one formant. Both levels are set equal so neither formant dominates.
- ASSIGN UNI: every note goes to both XM1 and XM2.
- XM1 level 5.5, XM2 level 5.5: 55 % each. XM1 comes down from 7 and XM2 up from 0.
- XM1 pan −1, XM2 pan +1: only 20 % to each side, so the two formants blend into one vowel rather than two sounds.
- Listen for: the note sounding from both modules, still the plain starting sawtooth.

steps.title: A rich source
steps.why:
Each module gets two slightly detuned sawtooths. A saw has every harmonic, so the filters in the next step have something to pick from.
- VCO 1 saw 80 %, VCO 2 saw 70 %: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. The knobs in the VCF (filter) section are silent at the centre and send the saw to the left.
- VCO 2 fine tune +0.4 (+8 cents): a slight detune, so each module beats gently, like several voices at once.
- Listen for: a thick, buzzy, slightly chorused tone.

steps.title: One formant per module
steps.why:
Each module’s VCF (voltage-controlled filter) is set to band-pass and tuned to one formant of “aah”. Neither follows the keys, so the vowel stays put while the melody moves.
- VCF response BP, both modules: band-pass keeps only the band around the cutoff.
- VCF resonance 5 (50 %): how sharp the formants are. Higher is more vocal but thinner.
- XM1 VCF frequency 5.2 (687 Hz): the first formant, about 700 Hz. Lower it towards 4 and the vowel moves towards “oh” and “oo”.
- XM2 VCF frequency 6 (1.2 kHz): the second formant, about 1,100 to 1,200 Hz. Raise it towards 7 and the vowel moves towards “eh” and “ee”.
- Listen for: the buzz turning into a wordless “aah”. Mute one module with its LEVEL and the vowel falls apart.

steps.title: Breathe and sing
steps.why:
ENV 1 makes each note breathe in and release slowly, and a small vibrato on all four oscillators makes it sound sung. Each module’s vibrato runs at its own speed, like different singers.
- ENV 1 A 420 ms, D 2.1 s, S 100 %: ENV 1, the loudness envelope, swells over nearly half a second, holds, and fades over 1.7 seconds.
- VCO 1 and 2 FM +0.2 st from LFO: left of centre moves pitch (FM means frequency modulation). A fifth of a semitone is a small vibrato; further left and the choir wobbles.
- XM1 LFO 4.41 Hz, XM2 5.00 Hz: the LFO (low-frequency oscillator) on each module, slightly different speeds.
- Listen for: a soft choir swelling in, with a gentle, uneven shimmer.

sounds.name: Overtone Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of overtone singing over a drone
sounds.blurb: A low, steady drone with a whistling melody of overtones drifting slowly above it.
sounds.how: Both VCAs are at ON/EXT, so the modules drone with no key held. XM1 is the warm base: a low fifth through a low-pass filter. XM2 plays the same note as a bright sawtooth through the band-pass filter with high resonance, which picks out one harmonic at a time. XM2’s slow LFO moves the band up and down, and the harmonics sing out one after another, as in overtone singing.

steps.title: Two drones
steps.why:
Both modules are made to sound all the time, so a key only changes the note. That is the base for a drone.
- XM1 and XM2 VCA mode ON/EXT: the VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) is the volume stage. At ENV it opens only while ENV 1 runs on a note; at ON/EXT it stays open, unless a cable in VCA CV takes over.
- XM2 level 6 (60 %): XM2 starts at 0; at 6 it sits a little under XM1.
- XM1 pan −2, XM2 pan +2.5: 40 % left and 50 % right, so the base and the overtones sit apart.
- Listen for: both modules sounding straight away, with no key held.

steps.title: XM1: a low fifth
steps.why:
XM1 becomes the warm base: a low fifth, rounded off by the filter.
- VCO 1 −4 (saw 80 %), VCO 2 −3 (saw 60 %): VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. The knobs in the VCF (filter) section send the saw to the left.
- VCO 2 frequency 6.2 (+7 st): a fifth up. The knob is continuous, so the fifth sits at about 6.17.
- FREQ 4 (304 Hz), RES 2: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, set low, so the base is dark and round.
- Listen for: a warm, open fifth under XM2’s still-bright sawtooth.

steps.title: XM2: a band-pass that picks harmonics
steps.why:
XM2 plays the same note through a narrow, resonant band-pass filter, which picks out one or two harmonics of the note at a time.
- XM2 VCO 1 into VCF −5 (saw 100 %): the full sawtooth, which has every harmonic for the filter to pick from.
- XM2 VCF response BP: band-pass lets through only a band around the cutoff.
- XM2 VCF resonance 8.5 (85 %): how narrow the band is. High enough and single harmonics whistle out.
- XM2 VCF frequency 6 (1.2 kHz): the middle of the overtone range.
- Listen for: a whistling tone above the drone. Turn XM2’s FREQUENCY slowly by hand and hear it step from one harmonic to the next.

steps.title: Let the LFO sing
steps.why:
XM2’s LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves a setting) now moves the band up and down, and the harmonics sing out one after another, as in overtone singing.
- XM2 VCF modulation source LFO: the switch under the filter’s MODULATION knob. It starts at ENV 2.
- XM2 VCF modulation +2.2 (+2.0 oct): how far up and down the band moves, about two octaves.
- XM2 LFO rate 1.5 (0.26 Hz): one sweep about every four seconds. Slower makes each harmonic hang longer.
- Listen for: a slow, whistled melody of overtones over the drone. Change the key and the melody moves to the new note’s harmonics.

sounds.name: Airy Octave Pad
sounds.ref: Two modules an octave apart, each filtered differently
sounds.blurb: A wide, breathing pad: a warm body on one side and an airy, shimmering octave on the other.
sounds.how: UNI plays each note on both modules. XM1 plays it as a warm, low-passed pulse and sawtooth. XM2 plays it an octave up through its filter with NOTCH turned most of the way towards high-pass, which removes the body and leaves only air and shimmer. On both, the LFO slowly moves the pulse width, at different speeds on each module, so the pad keeps moving.

steps.title: Both modules, wide apart
steps.why:
UNI plays every note on both modules, and they are panned well apart: a warm body will sit on one side and an airy octave on the other.
- ASSIGN UNI: both XM1 and XM2 play each note. It is where the switch starts.
- XM2 level 6 (60 %): up from 0, a little under XM1’s 7, as XM2 will be the lighter top layer.
- XM1 pan −3, XM2 pan +3: 60 % to each side, for a wide pad.
- Listen for: the note sounding from both sides, still the plain starting sawtooth on each.

steps.title: Pulse and sawtooth, XM2 an octave up
steps.why:
Each module gets a pulse and a sawtooth, a few cents apart, and XM2 is moved up an octave.
- VCO 1 pulse 60 %, VCO 2 saw 60 %: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. The knobs in the VCF (filter) section are silent at the centre, saw to the left, pulse to the right. The pulse is a square at its starting 50 % width, hollow; the saw adds buzz.
- VCO 2 fine tune +0.5 (+10 cents): a slight detune on each module, so the pair beats slowly.
- XM2 VCO 1 and VCO 2 frequency 7 (+12 st): XM2 an octave above XM1. On FREQUENCY two numbers is an octave.
- Listen for: a fuller, gently moving note with a brighter octave on the right.

steps.title: Slow pulse-width movement
steps.why:
PWM (pulse-width modulation) gives the pad a slow shimmer: each module’s LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves a setting) keeps changing the width of VCO 1’s pulse.
- VCO 1 modulation +2 (PWM 32 %): right of centre moves pulse width rather than pitch. More gives a deeper sweep.
- VCO 1 modulation source LFO: the switch starts at ENV 1; at LFO the width moves continuously.
- XM1 LFO 0.75 Hz, XM2 1.10 Hz: XM2’s runs a little faster, so the two sides never line up.
- Listen for: a slow, choral movement in the tone, different on each side. Set VCO 1 modulation to the centre on one module to hear its side go still.

steps.title: Warm below, air above
steps.why:
Now the two modules are filtered differently: XM1 warm and rounded, XM2 stripped of its body so only air and shimmer are left on top.
- XM1 FREQ 5 (600 Hz), RES 1.5: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, fairly low, for a warm body.
- XM2 VCF notch +2 (30 % LP, 70 % HP): the SEM’s NOTCH knob sweeps from low-pass through notch to high-pass. Turned right like this it is mostly high-pass, which removes the body. Turn it left and XM2 fills out.
- XM2 FREQ 5.5 (843 Hz), RES 2: where XM2’s cut sits, so only the upper part of its octave remains.
- Listen for: a warm tone on the left and a thin, breathy shimmer on the right. Pull XM2 level down to hear how much air it adds.

steps.title: Slow in, slow out
steps.why:
ENV 1, the loudness envelope, makes the pad swell in slowly and fade out slowly, so chords overlap and breathe.
- ENV 1 attack 7.5 (900 ms), both modules: nearly a second to reach full level.
- ENV 1 decay 7.5 (3.0 s, release 2.4 s): with full sustain it only acts after you let go. On the SEM DECAY also sets the release, so chords fade over more than two seconds.
- ENV 1 sustain 10 (100 %): full level while held.
- Listen for: chords rising gently and hanging after you let go. Change chords before the tail ends and they blend.

sounds.name: Wide Chorus Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of late-1970s ensemble pads
sounds.blurb: A lush, wide pad in which four sawtooths drift slowly against each other.
sounds.how: UNI plays every note on both modules, panned wide apart. On each module, VCO 2’s pitch is moved very slightly by the LFO, so it drifts in and out of tune with VCO 1. The two LFOs run at different speeds, so the drifting on the left never matches the right, and the pad sounds wide and alive, the way a chorus effect does.

steps.title: Both modules, panned wide apart
steps.why:
UNI plays every note on both modules, and they are panned wide apart, so two separate pairs of oscillators can drift on each side.
- ASSIGN UNI: both XM1 and XM2 play each note. It is where the switch starts.
- XM2 level 7 (70 %): up from 0, matching XM1.
- XM1 pan −4, XM2 pan +4: 80 % to each side, so the left and right drifting pairs are heard apart.
- Listen for: the note from both speakers, still the plain starting sawtooth.

steps.title: Four sawtooths
steps.why:
All four VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) go in as sawtooths, the brightest, fullest raw material and the classic basis of an ensemble pad.
- VCO 1 and VCO 2 −4 (saw 80 %): the knobs in the VCF (filter) section are silent at the centre and send the saw to the left.
- Listen for: a loud, buzzy note. The four saws are all in tune for now, so it sounds static; the next step sets them drifting.

steps.title: VCO 2 drifts on each module
steps.why:
On each module the LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves a setting) moves VCO 2’s pitch very slightly, so it drifts in and out of tune with VCO 1, like a chorus effect.
- VCO 2 modulation −0.5 (FM +0.2 st): left of centre moves pitch (FREQ; FM means frequency modulation). A fifth of a semitone is a gentle drift; further left and the pad goes seasick.
- VCO 2 modulation source LFO: the switch starts at ENV 2.
- XM1 LFO 0.66 Hz, XM2 0.97 Hz: the speed of the drift on the left and right. They differ, so the two sides never match.
- Listen for: a wide, swirling pad that moves differently on each side. Set one module’s VCO 2 modulation to the centre and that side goes flat.

steps.title: Warm and slow
steps.why:
The filter warms the four saws and opens a little as each note grows, and ENV 1 makes every note swell in and fade slowly.
- FREQ 4.8 (524 Hz), RES 1.5: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, part way down. This is the warmth of the pad.
- ENV 2 A 610 ms, D 2.1 s, S 70 %: with VCF MOD at +1.5 (up to 1.2 octaves), ENV 2, the filter envelope, opens the filter slowly, then settles most of the way up.
- ENV 1 A 610 ms, D 2.6 s, S 100 %: ENV 1, the loudness envelope, swells in over half a second and fades over two after you let go.
- Listen for: soft chords that bloom and hang. Play a slow progression and let each chord overlap the next.

sounds.name: Cello and Violin Duet
sounds.ref: SPLIT: two bowed instruments, one per hand
sounds.blurb: Two bowed string lines, a warm cello on the left and a brighter violin on the right.
sounds.how: SPLIT gives keys below middle C to XM1 and the rest to XM2, so each hand plays its own instrument. Both are sawtooths with a soft bow and a vibrato, but XM1 is darker, with a slower vibrato, and XM2 is brighter, with a faster one. Two separate voices let two lines move independently, each with its own tone and its own place in the stereo.

steps.title: Split the keyboard
steps.why:
SPLIT turns the two modules into two instruments, one for each hand: a cello on XM1 below middle C and a violin on XM2 above it.
- ASSIGN SPLIT: keys below middle C play XM1, the rest play XM2.
- XM2 level 6.5 (65 %): XM2 starts at 0; at 6.5 it sits just under XM1.
- XM1 pan −3, XM2 pan +3: 60 % to each side, so the two lines have their own places, like two players on a stage.
- Listen for: low and high keys coming from opposite sides, still the plain starting sawtooth.

steps.title: Two bowed sawtooths
steps.why:
Both instruments start from two slightly detuned sawtooths, with a soft bow at the start of each note. The settings are the same on both modules; the next steps make them different.
- Saws 80 % and 60 %, +8 cents: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. A saw is the closest simple wave to a bowed string; the detune adds movement.
- ENV 1 A 250 ms, D 1.5 s, S 90 %: ENV 1, the loudness envelope, is the bow: a quarter of a second to speak, then a 1.2 s release.
- VCF MOD +0.8 oct, ENV 2 slow: ENV 2 (attack 200 ms, decay 1.5 s, sustain 70 %) opens the VCF (filter) a little as the bow gets going.
- Listen for: notes that start softly, as if bowed, and ring briefly after you let go.

steps.title: A dark cello, a bright violin
steps.why:
The two filters give the instruments their different characters: XM1 dark and warm, XM2 brighter and edgier.
- XM1 FREQ 4.3 (373 Hz), RES 1.5: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, set low for a cello’s warmth.
- XM2 FREQ 5.6 (902 Hz), RES 1.5: higher, for the violin’s brightness and bite.
- Listen for: the left hand now round and mellow, the right hand thinner and brighter. Swap the two FREQUENCY values to hear why it matters.

steps.title: Two vibratos
steps.why:
Each instrument gets its own vibrato. The cello’s is slower and the violin’s faster, as a cellist and a violinist would play.
- VCO 1 and 2 MOD −0.5 (FM +0.2 st): left of centre moves pitch (FM means frequency modulation). A fifth of a semitone is a gentle vibrato; further left gets wobbly.
- Modulation sources LFO: each VCO’s switch set to LFO (low-frequency oscillator), a slow wave that moves the pitch.
- XM1 LFO 3.65 Hz, XM2 5.33 Hz: about three and a half wobbles a second on the cello, five on the violin.
- Listen for: two lines, each with its own waver. Play them together and hear that they do not shake in step.

sounds.name: Two Flutes
sounds.ref: In the style of a flute duet in thirds
sounds.blurb: Two breathy flutes playing a melody in thirds, one on each side.
sounds.how: A square wave through a low filter is close to a flute’s soft, hollow tone, and a little white noise through the same filter is the breath. A slight attack and a gentle vibrato make each note blown rather than switched on. DUO gives each flute its own module and its own side.

steps.title: Two flutes
steps.why:
Two flutes need two voices. DUO plays each note of a third on its own module, and the modules are panned apart like two players.
- ASSIGN DUO: each new key goes to whichever module is free, so two held notes sound together, one per module.
- XM2 level 7 (70 %): XM2 starts at 0; at 7 it matches XM1.
- XM1 pan −2.5, XM2 pan +2.5: 50 % to each side.
- Listen for: hold two keys and hear one on each side, still the plain starting sawtooth.

steps.title: A square and a breath of noise
steps.why:
A square wave is close to a flute’s soft, hollow tone, and a touch of white noise is the breath.
- VCO 1 +4 (pulse 80 %), PW 50 %: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. Right of centre in the VCF (filter) section sends the pulse; at 50 % it is a square.
- EXT/noise knob +1 (noise 20 %): the third knob in the VCF section is silent at the centre, brings in the external input to the left and white noise to the right. Further right is breathier; at the centre the flute is pure.
- Listen for: a hollow tone with a faint hiss. It is still too bright; the filter comes next.

steps.title: A soft filter
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) rounds off the square and the breath together, so the tone is soft and the hiss sits inside it.
- VCF frequency 5 (600 Hz): low-pass, low enough to round off the square. Higher sounds more like a recorder; lower, muffled.
- VCF resonance 1.5 (15 %): a slight lift at the cutoff for a little body.
- Listen for: a soft, dark flute with a breathy edge. Sweep FREQUENCY to hear it move from flute to recorder.

steps.title: Blown notes with vibrato
steps.why:
ENV 1, the loudness envelope, makes notes start with a breath, and a gentle vibrato from the LFO makes them sound blown.
- ENV 1 attack 4.8 (120 ms): the breath at the start of each note.
- ENV 1 D 720 ms, S 90 %: a slight settle after the start, then a soft tail after you let go.
- VCO 1 FM +0.2 st from LFO: left of centre moves pitch (FM means frequency modulation), a small vibrato from the LFO (low-frequency oscillator).
- XM1 LFO 4.41 Hz, XM2 5.00 Hz: XM2 a touch faster, so the flutes do not waver in step.
- Listen for: two breathy flutes in thirds, each with its own vibrato.

sounds.name: Talking Filter Riff
sounds.ref: In the style of Daft Punk — "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger"
sounds.blurb: A short, chopped synth riff whose filters open like a mouth on every note, so it almost seems to say something.
sounds.how: UNI plays every note on both modules, and each module filters it differently. XM1’s filter is set to band-pass with plenty of resonance, and ENV 2 sweeps it up and back down on each note, which sounds like a vowel changing from “oo” to “ah”. XM2’s filter sits at the notch, which cuts a slice out of the middle of the sound, and its own ENV 2 moves that slice. Short notes that stop quickly give the chopped, cut-up feel.

steps.title: Both modules on every note
steps.why:
UNI plays every note on both modules, and each module will filter it differently. Panning them slightly apart lets you hear each filter on its own side.
- ASSIGN UNI: every note goes to both XM1 and XM2. It is where the switch starts.
- XM1 level 6, XM2 level 6: 60 % each. XM1 comes down from 7 and XM2 up from 0, so the two match.
- XM1 pan −1.5, XM2 pan +1.5: 30 % to each side.
- Listen for: the note sounding from both modules, still the plain starting sawtooth.

steps.title: A buzzy source
steps.why:
Each module gets a sawtooth and a square, slightly detuned. A filter can only pick out harmonics that are there, and this mix is full of them.
- VCO 1 −4 (saw 80 %), both modules: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. Left of centre on its knob in the VCF (filter) section sends the saw.
- VCO 2 +3.5 (pulse 70 %): right of centre sends the pulse, a square at its starting 50 % width.
- VCO 2 fine tune +0.3 (+6 cents): a few cents sharp, so the pair beats gently.
- Listen for: a loud, buzzy, slightly moving tone.

steps.title: A band-pass that talks
steps.why:
XM1’s filter becomes the mouth. A narrow, resonant band-pass that jumps up and falls back on each note sounds like a vowel changing from “oo” to “ah”.
- XM1 VCF response BP: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) keeps only a narrow band around the cutoff, which is what makes it sound like a voice.
- XM1 VCF resonance 6 (60 %): how sharp and vocal the band is. Lower it and the talking fades into a plain filter sweep.
- XM1 VCF frequency 4.6 (457 Hz): the resting vowel, a dark “oo”.
- XM1 VCF modulation +2.5 (+2.5 oct): how far the vowel moves on each note.
- ENV 2 A 0, D 280 ms, S 20 %: ENV 2, the filter envelope, snaps the band up and lets it fall back in about a quarter of a second. That is how quickly the mouth closes.
- Listen for: a “wow” at the start of every note, on the left.

steps.title: A moving notch on XM2
steps.why:
XM2’s filter is set to the notch, which removes a band instead of keeping one, and its own ENV 2 moves that gap on each note.
- XM2 VCF notch 0 (notch): the SEM’s NOTCH knob sweeps from low-pass through notch to high-pass; at the centre it cuts a slice out of the sound.
- XM2 FREQ 5.4 (788 Hz), RES 3: where the slice sits, with a little emphasis on its edges.
- XM2 ENV 2 A 0, D 210 ms, S 0: with XM2 VCF MOD at +1.8 (up to 1.5 octaves), the gap jumps up on each note and falls back in about a fifth of a second.
- Listen for: a hollow, phasey edge on the right against XM1’s vowel. Pull XM2 level down to compare.

steps.title: Chop the notes
steps.why:
ENV 1, the loudness envelope, is shortened on both modules so each note stops almost as soon as you let go: the chopped, cut-up feel.
- ENV 1 attack 0 (3 ms): notes start at once, on the beat.
- ENV 1 decay 3.4 (160 ms, release 120 ms): on the SEM DECAY is the release as well. Short keeps notes clipped; higher values smear them together.
- ENV 1 sustain 7 (70 %): held notes dip slightly after the start, which helps the “wow” stand out.
- Listen for: a tight, stuttering riff with gaps between the notes. Play it staccato and hear each note talk and stop.

sounds.name: Clipped Robot Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Kraftwerk — "The Robots"
sounds.blurb: A hard, clipped square-wave bass that plays in strict, mechanical time, with a small click on the front of every note.
sounds.how: XM1 is the body of the bass: two square waves an octave apart through a low-pass filter, with both envelopes at no sustain, so every note is the same short, clipped length however long the key is held. XM2 plays each note too, in UNI, but as a thin pulse an octave up through the high-pass end of its filter with an even shorter envelope: a click that marks the start of each note. Nothing wobbles or slides, which keeps it rigid.

steps.title: Two squares, an octave apart
steps.why:
XM1 becomes the body of the bass: two square waves an octave apart. A square is hollow and has fewer harmonics than a saw, which suits a rigid, electronic bass.
- VCO 1 pulse 80 %, VCO 2 pulse 70 %: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. On the knobs in the VCF (filter) section, right of centre sends the pulse.
- VCO 1 and VCO 2 pulse width 50 %: exactly square, hollow like a clarinet. Narrower would be more nasal.
- VCO 2 frequency 3 (−12 st): an octave below VCO 1, for weight.
- Listen for: a loud, hollow, organ-like bass tone that holds while the key is down.

steps.title: A dark filter with a snap
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) goes dark, and ENV 2, the filter envelope, gives each note a quick bright edge that closes at once.
- VCF frequency 4 (304 Hz): low-pass, so the body of the bass is dark.
- VCF resonance 3 (30 %): a small lift at the cutoff for a slightly firmer snap.
- VCF modulation +2 (+1.8 oct): how far ENV 2 opens the filter at the start of each note: the snap.
- ENV 2 A 0, D 160 ms, S 0: opens at once and shuts in about a sixth of a second.
- Listen for: a short “dit” of brightness on each note, then a dark, held tone.

steps.title: Clip every note
steps.why:
ENV 1, the loudness envelope, is set with no sustain, so every note dies away after the same short time however long the key is held. That is what makes the line sound exact and machine-like.
- ENV 1 attack 0 (3 ms): each note starts on the beat.
- ENV 1 decay 3.8 (210 ms, release 160 ms): the length of each note. Keep it shorter than the gap between notes.
- ENV 1 sustain 0: at 0 every note is clipped to the same length. Raise it and held notes ring on, which loses the rigid feel.
- Listen for: short, identical notes, whether you tap or hold the keys.

steps.title: A click on top from XM2
steps.why:
XM2 plays every note too and adds a click on top: a thin pulse an octave up, through the high-pass end of its filter, with a very short envelope. It helps the bass cut through a mix.
- ASSIGN UNI: both modules play each note.
- XM2 level 3.5 (35 %): quiet. Too high and it turns into a second, buzzy part.
- XM2 VCO 1 PW 20 %, +12 st: VCO 1 at +4 on its knob (pulse 80 %), a narrow, nasal pulse an octave up.
- XM2 NOTCH +5, FREQ 6 (1.2 kHz): the SEM’s NOTCH knob fully right is high-pass, so only the top of the sound gets through.
- XM2 ENV 1 A 0, D 68 ms, S 0: the click lasts about a fifteenth of a second.
- Listen for: a small tick at the front of each note. Pull XM2 level to 0 and the bass gets duller and harder to place.

sounds.name: Rubber Glide Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernie Worrell — "One Nation Under a Groove" (Funkadelic)
sounds.blurb: A squelchy, bouncing funk lead that slides into every note, with a round octave underneath.
sounds.how: XM1 carries the tone: a sawtooth and a narrow pulse through a resonant low-pass filter that ENV 2 flicks open on each note, which gives the squelch. XM2 plays the same note an octave down as a dark square, so the line has weight. Portamento on both modules makes every note slide in from the last one, which is what makes it sound rubbery.

steps.title: A sawtooth and a thin pulse
steps.why:
XM1 carries the tone: a sawtooth with a thin pulse beside it. The mix is bright and buzzy, which gives the filter something to chew on.
- VCO 1 into VCF −4 (saw 80 %): VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. Left of centre on its knob in the VCF (filter) section sends the saw.
- VCO 2 +3 (pulse 60 %), PW 30 %: a narrow pulse, which adds a nasal edge to the saw.
- VCO 2 fine tune +0.3 (+6 cents): a few cents sharp, so the pair beats and sounds thicker.
- Listen for: a bright, reedy buzz with a slow wobble.

steps.title: A resonant filter that snaps open
steps.why:
A resonant filter that ENV 2 throws open on every note gives the squelch, the wet “yow” of a funk lead.
- VCF frequency 3.8 (265 Hz): the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, set low so the note is dark between yows.
- VCF resonance 6.5 (65 %): the squelch. The SEM filter stays round even here. Lower it and the line turns into a plain, polite lead.
- VCF modulation +3 (+3.3 oct): how far ENV 2, the filter envelope, throws the filter open at the start of each note.
- ENV 2 A 0, D 330 ms, S 20 %: opens at once, falls back over a third of a second, and holds a little open.
- Listen for: a wet “yow” on every note. Sweep ENV 2 decay to make it shorter and snappier or longer and lazier.

steps.title: Short, punchy notes
steps.why:
ENV 1, the loudness envelope, is set for short, punchy notes: full straight away, held while the key is down, and stopping quickly when you let go.
- ENV 1 attack 0 (3 ms): each note lands on the beat.
- ENV 1 decay 3.8 (210 ms, release 160 ms): after the start, the level settles in about a fifth of a second. On the SEM DECAY also sets the release, so notes stop quickly and the rests in the riff stay clean.
- ENV 1 sustain 8 (80 %): held notes stay up, so long notes keep their squelch.
- Listen for: a bouncy riff with clean gaps between the notes.

steps.title: An octave underneath from XM2
steps.why:
XM2 plays the same note an octave down as a dark square, so the line has weight without blurring the squelch on top.
- ASSIGN UNI: both modules play each note. It is where the switch starts.
- XM2 level 5 (50 %): how much of the octave underneath you hear.
- XM2 VCO 1 pulse 80 %, −12 st: a square, an octave below XM1.
- XM2 FREQ 4.2 (348 Hz), RES 2: a darker filter with only a small ENV 2 lift (VCF MOD +1.2 octaves, decay 250 ms, sustain 20 %).
- XM2 ENV 1 D 210 ms, S 80 %: the same loudness shape as XM1, so the two start and stop together.
- Listen for: the lead gaining a round bottom. Pull XM2 level to 0 to hear how thin XM1 is on its own.

steps.title: Slide into every note
steps.why:
Portamento makes every note slide in from the one before, which is what makes the lead sound rubbery.
- Portamento ON: turns on the slides on both modules.
- XM1 and XM2 portamento 2.5 (190 ms): a fifth of a second per slide, up or down. Higher gives a slower, lazier slide. Keep the two the same so the octave slides together.
- Listen for: every note bending in quickly from the last. Play the riff legato and hear it bounce and squelch in the style of a Bernie Worrell funk lead.

sounds.name: Sombre Low Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Eno — David Bowie, "Warszawa" (Low)
sounds.blurb: A dark, slow pad with a hollow, voice-like tone on top, for slow minor melodies.
sounds.how: Both modules play every note. XM1 is the body: a sawtooth and a square an octave below it through a low-pass filter, both swelling in slowly. XM2 goes through the band-pass filter, which keeps only a narrow band and sounds like a hollow “oo”, with a slow vibrato on it. Long attacks and long release let each note grow and fade, so a slow line joins up.

steps.title: A dark body on XM1
steps.why:
XM1 becomes the body: a sawtooth with a square an octave below it, through a low filter, for a deep, rounded note.
- VCO 1 into VCF −3.5 (saw 70 %): VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. Left of centre on its knob in the VCF (filter) section sends the saw.
- VCO 2 +3.5 (pulse 70 %), FREQ 3 (−12 st): a square (pulse at its starting 50 %), an octave below VCO 1 for depth.
- FREQ 4 (304 Hz), RES 2: the VCF (voltage-controlled filter) in low-pass, set low to keep the body dark.
- Listen for: a deep, soft, rounded note with no bright edge.

steps.title: Slow swell
steps.why:
ENV 1 and ENV 2 are slowed right down, so each note swells in, opens a little and fades slowly into the next.
- ENV 1 attack 6.8 (530 ms): ENV 1, the loudness envelope, takes half a second to reach full level. Shorter and the pad starts to sound like an organ.
- ENV 1 D 3.0 s, S 100 %: full level while held; on the SEM DECAY is also the release, so notes fade slowly into the next one.
- VCF modulation +1.5 (+1.2 oct): how far ENV 2, the filter envelope, opens the filter.
- ENV 2 A 610 ms, D 3.0 s, S 60 %: the filter opens with the swell and settles part way.
- Listen for: each note growing out of silence and brightening slightly as it does.

steps.title: A hollow voice on XM2
steps.why:
XM2 plays every note too, through the band-pass filter, which keeps only a narrow band in the middle of the sound: a hollow, sung “oo”.
- ASSIGN UNI, XM2 level 5 (50 %): both modules on each note, XM2 brought in from 0.
- XM2 two saws 80 %, −8 cents: two saws slightly apart, full of harmonics.
- XM2 VCF response BP: band-pass is what gives XM2 its hollow, voice-like tone.
- XM2 FREQ 5 (600 Hz), RES 5: which vowel the voice sings. Lower is a darker “oo”, higher an “ah”.
- XM2 ENV 1 A 610 ms, D 3.0 s, S 100 %: the same slow swell and long fade as XM1.
- Listen for: a hollow “oo” floating above the dark body.

steps.title: A slow vibrato on the voice
steps.why:
XM2’s LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves a setting) adds a slow vibrato to the voice, while the body stays still.
- XM2 VCO 1 and 2 FM +0.3 st: left of centre moves pitch (FM means frequency modulation). A touch left is a gentle waver; further left gets unsteady.
- XM2 modulation sources LFO: both switches set to LFO.
- XM2 LFO rate 4 (1.25 Hz): a little over one waver a second, slow and sad rather than operatic.
- Listen for: the voice gently wavering over a steady body. Set XM2’s modulation knobs to the centre to hear it go still.

steps.title: Spread the two apart
steps.why:
The body and the voice are given their own places in the stereo, and XM1 is brought down a little, as two slow notes overlapping add up.
- XM1 pan −2, XM2 pan +2: 40 % to each side.
- XM1 level 6 (60 %): down from 7, so overlapping notes do not build up too loud and the voice sits on top.
- Listen for: the dark body on the left and the hollow voice on the right. Play a slow minor melody and let each note fade into the next, in the style of Eno’s “Warszawa”.

sounds.name: Steel Swell
sounds.ref: In the style of Daniel Lanois — "Frozen" (Belladonna)
sounds.blurb: A warm, soft lead that swells in on every note and bends up or down into the next, like a pedal steel.
sounds.how: The volume and the filter both rise slowly on each note, so there is no hard start: the note fades in, as a steel player does with a volume pedal. Portamento makes each new note bend in from the last. Both modules play every note, slightly out of tune with each other and panned apart, which makes the tone wide and warm.

steps.title: A soft square and a sawtooth
steps.why:
Each module starts with a soft square and a little sawtooth edge. XM2 is set up the same but stays silent until the last step, so for now only XM1 is heard.
- VCO 1 +3.5 (pulse 70 %), PW 50 %: VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator. Right of centre on its knob in the VCF (filter) section sends the pulse; at 50 % it is a square, round and hollow.
- VCO 2 into VCF −2 (saw 40 %): a little towards SAW, for some edge.
- VCO 2 fine tune +0.3 (+6 cents): a few cents sharp, so the pair beats slowly.
- Listen for: a round, hollow note with a slight buzz and a slow wobble.

steps.title: A warm filter that opens with the note
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) keeps the tone warm, and ENV 2 opens it slowly as each note grows, so the tone brightens with the swell.
- FREQ 4.6 (457 Hz), RES 2.5: low-pass, warm and rounded, with a slight lift at the cutoff.
- VCF modulation +1.2 (+0.8 oct): how far ENV 2, the filter envelope, opens the filter. Just right of centre, a small lift.
- ENV 2 A 610 ms, D 2.1 s, S 70 %: with VCF MOD at +1.2 (up to 0.8 octaves), ENV 2, the filter envelope, opens the filter slowly, then settles most of the way up.
- Listen for: each note starting dull and brightening over about half a second. The volume still starts hard; the next step changes that.

steps.title: Swell in every note
steps.why:
ENV 1, the loudness envelope, now fades each note in, as a steel player does with a volume pedal. There is no hard start any more.
- ENV 1 attack 7 (610 ms): about half a second to reach full level. Turn it down and the note starts hard, which loses the pedal-steel feel.
- ENV 1 decay 7 (2.1 s, release 1.7 s): with full sustain it only acts after you let go. On the SEM DECAY also sets the release, so notes fade slowly.
- ENV 1 sustain 10 (100 %): full level while held.
- Listen for: each note swelling in, with the tone opening at the same time.

steps.title: Bend into each note
steps.why:
Portamento makes each new note bend in from the last, like the steel bar moving along the strings.
- Portamento ON: turns the bends on for both modules.
- XM1 and XM2 portamento 3.5 (370 ms): a little over a third of a second per bend. Longer is a slower, more obvious slide.
- Listen for: play a slow melody legato and hear each note swell in while bending up or down from the one before.

steps.title: Two modules, wide and warm
steps.why:
XM2 now joins in, slightly out of tune with XM1 and panned the other way, which makes the tone wide and warm.
- ASSIGN UNI: both modules play every note. It is where the switch starts.
- XM2 level 6 (60 %): up from 0, a little under XM1.
- XM1 pan −2.5, XM2 pan +2.5: 50 % to each side, so the sound is wide.
- XM2 VCO 1 fine tune −0.3 (−7 cents): XM2 slightly flat against XM1, which makes the note slowly shimmer.
- Listen for: a wider, warmer swell that moves gently between the speakers, in the style of Daniel Lanois’s steel on “Frozen”.

- XM1 VCO 1 into the VCF +3 (pulse 60 %), VCO 2 into the VCF 0 (off), EXT/noise into the VCF +3 (noise 60 %)
- XM1 VCF response BP, VCF FREQUENCY 6.6 (1.8 kHz), VCF RESONANCE 4 (40 %)
- XM1 ENV 1 ATTACK 0 (3 ms), ENV 1 DECAY 1.5 (41 ms · release 30 ms), ENV 1 SUSTAIN 0 %
- Listen for: sharp, rattling clacks.

sounds.name: Gated Snare
sounds.ref: In the style of Peter Gabriel — "Intruder" (gated drums)
sounds.blurb: A huge, explosive snare cut off abruptly, the gated sound of the 80s.
sounds.how: Noise and a pulse, a flat envelope that holds full then cuts off sharply: a gate.

steps.title: Gated
steps.why:
- XM1 VCO 1 into the VCF +2.5 (pulse 50 %), VCO 2 into the VCF 0 (off), EXT/noise into the VCF +5 (noise 100 %)
- XM1 VCF FREQUENCY 6.4 (1.6 kHz), VCF RESONANCE 1 (10 %)
- XM1 ENV 1 ATTACK 0 (3 ms), ENV 1 DECAY 1.5 (41 ms · release 30 ms), ENV 1 SUSTAIN 10 (100 %): full, then the gate slams shut when the note ends.
- Listen for: a huge, abruptly cut snare.

sounds.name: Funky Bongos
sounds.ref: In the style of the Incredible Bongo Band — "Apache"
sounds.blurb: A pair of bright, pitched, popping hand drums, high and low.
sounds.how: DUO plays the two drums on the two modules, each with ENV 1 dropping its pitch a little through FM and a resonant snap.

steps.title: Two drums
steps.why:
- ASSIGN DUO, XM2 LEVEL 7 (70 %)
- XM1 VCO 1 into the VCF +3 (pulse 60 %), VCO 1 MOD source ENV 1, VCO 1 MODULATION −1.5 (FM +2.2 st)
- XM2 VCO 1 into the VCF +3 (pulse 60 %), VCO 1 MOD source ENV 1, VCO 1 MODULATION −1.5 (FM +2.2 st)
- XM1 VCF FREQUENCY 5 (600 Hz), XM2 VCF FREQUENCY 5 (600 Hz), XM1 VCF RESONANCE 3 (30 %), XM2 VCF RESONANCE 3 (30 %)
- XM1 ENV 1 DECAY 3.4 (160 ms · release 120 ms), XM2 ENV 1 DECAY 3.4 (160 ms · release 120 ms), XM1 ENV 1 SUSTAIN 0 %, XM2 ENV 1 SUSTAIN 0 %
- XM1 PAN −2 (left 40 %), XM2 PAN +2 (right 40 %)
- Listen for: popping, funky bongos.
